entities.span: The `/check review` that found this also raised three smaller items, recorded in `docs/reviews/2026-09-13-feat-spend-visibility-and-gating-polish.md` and deliberately NOT folded into this correction: the new function is `volatile` rather than `stable` (declaring it `stable` would make Postgres itself reject a write inside it, replacing a guarantee currently carried by a comment and a grep); no automated test forces its `configured: false` path; and two comments in `page.test.ts` cite `test/integration/usage-summary.test.ts`, which moved to `test/integration-serial/`. The first is a real hardening improvement and deserves its own pass.
Line references in this spec and elsewhere point into `src/app/(app)/search/page.tsx` by number. Step 8 moves that code. Re read them rather than trusting them once the revision lands
rejected_spans: the 2026-09-01 reflex about follow up items being the stalest part of a spec applies to these first.

entities.span: **Done 2026-09-13, and the item as written was wrong in both of its own particulars, which is the reflex proving itself.** It named spec 0013 as the other holder of these references: spec 0013 mentions `search/page.tsx` twice (`index.md:44` and `:187`) but never with a line number, and the numbered references outside this spec are spec 0015's, not 0013's. Its list `(154, 92, 94, 243)` was pre-correction and did not survive contact with the file either: a sweep of all of `docs/` for numeric references into that file found exactly four, and 154 and 92 were not among them, while 383 was and the item never listed it. The four, all re read against the file on 2026-09-13: this spec's `index.md:110`, the `hasQuery` conditional, 94 to **129**; this spec's `rationale.md:111`, the `Promise.all` over the applied and scoring reads inside `SearchOutcome`, 243 to **291**; and spec 0015's `index.md:211` and `verify.md:78`, both citing the `ScoredResults` index pairing (`const paired = listings.map(...)`), 383 to **442** in each.
rejected_spans: Corrected in the same pass rather than one at a time, per the 2026-08-31 reflex about fixing every instance of a claim that appears in more than one place.

entities.span: The `usage_cap` half of AC-10 corrects a string no user ever sees (`NON_PERSONAL_TABLES[].why`, read only by `stored-fields.test.ts`). Worth asking separately whether that registry should reach `/privacy` at all, or whether its `why` field is documentation for the codebase and should say so. Not decided here.
The retention rule spec 0011's own follow up flagged for `usage_gate_counter` (rows accumulate with no pruning) stays open.
rejected_spans: It is a privacy and storage question in its own right and deserves its own deliberate pass rather than riding along on this feature's read path.

entities.span: If a future feature shows `ai_scoring` or `ai_check` usage too, revisit where it lives: this spec kept it on `/search` deliberately
